events.title: The Roman army proclaims Jovian emperor after Julian's death
events.description: After Emperor Julian was killed in battle on his Persian expedition, the Roman army declared Jovian, of the imperial bodyguard, his successor. Jovian then made a peace that let the Sasanian Empire under Shapur II recover Nisibis and other territories.

events.title: Agatho begins his pontificate as bishop of Rome
events.description: Agatho became bishop of Rome, serving until his death in 681. During his tenure the Sixth Ecumenical Council was convened to deal with monothelitism, and he is venerated as a saint by both the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.

events.title: The Stratford Martyrs are burned for their Protestant beliefs
events.description: Eleven men and two women, the Stratford Martyrs, were burned at the stake together for their Protestant beliefs during the Marian persecutions, at Stratford-le-Bow or Stratford, Essex, both near London.
events.html: Eleven men and two women, the Stratford Martyrs, were burned at the stake together for their Protestant beliefs during the Marian persecutions, at Stratford-le-Bow or Stratford, Essex, both near London.

events.title: George II leads his army to victory at Dettingen
events.description: In the War of the Austrian Succession, an allied army under George II beat the French in Bavaria. It was the last time a reigning British monarch commanded troops in battle.
events.html: In the War of the Austrian Succession, an allied army under George II beat the French in Bavaria. It was the last time a reigning British monarch commanded troops in battle.

events.title: Mormon founder Joseph Smith is killed by a mob
events.description: Militiamen stormed the jail in Carthage, Illinois, where Smith and his brother Hyrum were held, and shot them dead. Brigham Young later led most of his followers west to Utah.

events.title: Sailors mutiny aboard the battleship Potemkin
events.description: Crew of the Russian Black Sea Fleet battleship rose against their officers after a dispute over rotten meat. The mutiny became a symbol of the 1905 Revolution, later immortalised by Eisenstein.

events.title: UN Security Council calls on members to defend South Korea
events.description: Resolution 83 recommended that members help South Korea repel the North's attack. The Soviet Union was boycotting the Council and could not veto it.

events.title: Gordon Brown succeeds Tony Blair as Prime Minister
events.description: After ten years as Chancellor, Gordon Brown became Prime Minister. His premiership was dominated by the global financial crisis of 2008.
